question: President of India, Droupadi Murmu presented the ________ of the Digital India Awards on 7th January 2023 in New Delhi.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 7th edition.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• President Droupadi Murmu presented the 7th edition of the Digital India Awards (Digital India Awards 2022) on 7 January 2023 at Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi. (डिजिटल इंडिया पुरस्कार — 7वां संस्करण)

 

• The Digital India Awards are given by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) to recognise and promote excellence in digital governance initiatives by government bodies, PSUs and startups.

 

• The awards were first instituted in 2016 to encourage innovative use of technology in citizen-centric governance, and are presented periodically to mark milestones under the Digital India programme, launched in 2015.

 

• The theme for the 2022 edition centred on citizen-centric digital initiatives that improved ease of living and ease of doing business.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Digital India programme was launched on 1 July 2015 with the vision of transforming India into a digitally empowered society and knowledge economy.

 

• Flagship digital initiatives recognised under such awards include DigiLocker, UMANG, e-Gov mobile apps and Common Service Centres (CSCs).

 

NOTE

 

• 8th edition (Option 1): Incorrect; the count had reached the 7th edition by January 2023.

 

• 5th edition (Option 2): Incorrect; understates the actual edition number.

 

• 6th edition (Option 4): Incorrect; the 2022 awards ceremony held in January 2023 was the 7th, not the 6th, edition.

question: In January 2022, who was named for the Rachael Heyhoe Flint Trophy for ICC Women's Cricketer of the Year?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Smriti Mandhana.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Indian cricketer Smriti Mandhana was awarded the Rachael Heyhoe Flint Trophy for ICC Women's Cricketer of the Year in January 2022, for her performances through 2021. (स्मृति मंधाना — ICC महिला क्रिकेटर ऑफ द ईयर)

 

• The award is named after Rachael Heyhoe Flint, the legendary former England women's cricket captain, and is presented annually as part of the ICC Awards.

 

• Mandhana became only the second Indian cricketer (after Mithali Raj, who won the inaugural edition in 2018) to receive this honour.

 

• She also won the ICC Women's ODI Cricketer of the Year award for 2021 in the same annual awards cycle.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The men's equivalent of the ICC Cricketer of the Year award is the Sir Garfield Sobers Trophy.

 

• Smriti Mandhana is a left-handed opening batter from Maharashtra and has captained the Indian women's ODI team.

 

NOTE

 

• Mithali Raj (Option 1): Former Indian captain; she won the inaugural Rachael Heyhoe Flint Trophy in 2018, not 2022.

 

• Elyse Perry (Option 2): Australian all-rounder; a past ICC award winner but not the 2021/2022 recipient of this trophy.

 

• Lizelle Lee (Option 3): South African wicketkeeper-batter; not the recipient of this award.

question: The chemical formula of propene is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is C₃H₆.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Propene (propylene) is an unsaturated hydrocarbon with the molecular formula C₃H₆, structurally CH₂=CH-CH₃. (प्रोपीन — C₃H₆)

 

• It belongs to the alkene (olefin) family of hydrocarbons, which have the general formula CₙH₂ₙ and contain one carbon-carbon double bond.

 

• Propene is one of the simplest alkenes after ethene (C₂H₄) and is a key petrochemical feedstock used to manufacture polypropylene.

 

• It is obtained mainly as a by-product of petroleum refining and steam cracking of hydrocarbons like naphtha.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Ethene (C₂H₄) is the simplest alkene and is used to make polyethylene.

 

• Alkynes have the general formula CₙH₂ₙ₋₂ and contain a triple bond, e.g. ethyne (acetylene), C₂H₂.

 

NOTE

 

• C₂H₄ (Option 1): This is ethene, not propene.

 

• C₃H₄ (Option 2): This is propyne, an alkyne, not propene.

 

• C₂H₂ (Option 4): This is ethyne (acetylene), an alkyne with a triple bond.

question: Which of the following is the closest wild relative of domestic cattle protected in some of the famous national parks of India like Nagarhole and Bandipur?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gaur.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Gaur (Bos gaurus), also called the Indian bison, is the largest extant wild bovine and is considered the closest wild relative of domestic cattle. (गौर — जंगली मवेशी का निकटतम रिश्तेदार)

 

• Gaurs are protected in several famous national parks and tiger reserves of India, including Nagarhole and Bandipur in Karnataka, as well as Bandhavgarh, Kanha and Periyar.

 

• They are listed as Vulnerable on the IUCN Red List and are protected under Schedule I of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972.

 

• Gaurs are herbivorous, live in herds, and are found across the forests of the Western Ghats, Central India and the Northeast.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Nagarhole and Bandipur National Parks, along with Mudumalai and Wayanad, form part of the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve, one of India's richest wildlife habitats.

 

• The Gaur is Karnataka's state animal.

 

NOTE

 

• Red angus (Option 1): A domestic cattle breed developed in the USA/Scotland, not a wild relative.

 

• Asiatic buffalo (Option 2): Refers to the wild water buffalo (Arni), a different wild bovine, not the closest relative of domestic cattle.

 

• Nilgai (Option 3): The largest Asian antelope, not a bovine and not closely related to domestic cattle.

question: An annual statement of the estimated receipts and expenditure of the government over the fiscal year is known as ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Budget.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Budget is the annual financial statement of the estimated receipts and expenditure of the government for a fiscal year. (बजट — वार्षिक वित्तीय विवरण)

 

• In India, the Budget is presented under Article 112 of the Constitution, which mandates the 'Annual Financial Statement' to be laid before Parliament.

 

• It is prepared by the Ministry of Finance and presented by the Finance Minister, generally on 1 February each year, covering the fiscal year from 1 April to 31 March.

 

• The Budget comprises the Revenue Budget (revenue receipts and expenditure) and the Capital Budget (capital receipts and expenditure).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Union Budget is now presented as a paperless Budget since 2021, following the merger of the Railway Budget with the General Budget from 2017.

 

• The Economic Survey is presented a day before the Union Budget and reviews the country's economic performance.

 

NOTE

 

• Income sheet (Option 1): Not a recognised term for the government's annual financial statement.

 

• Plan (Option 2): Refers to development/Five-Year Plans, not the annual receipts-expenditure statement.

 

• Account (Option 3): Too generic; does not specifically denote the annual estimated receipts and expenditure statement.

question: What is the name of the scheme launched to fund infrastructure and social development projects in the Northeast for a period of four years from 2022-23 to 2025-26?
solution_text:
The correct answer is PM-DevINE.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• PM-DevINE (Prime Minister's Development Initiative for North East Region) was announced in the Union Budget 2022-23 to fund infrastructure and social development projects in the Northeast. (पीएम-डिवाइन — पूर्वोत्तर विकास योजना)

 

• It is a new Central Sector Scheme implemented by the Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region (DoNER), with 100% central funding, for the period 2022-23 to 2025-26.

 

• It aims to fund infrastructure (in the spirit of PM GatiShakti), support industries, promote social development projects, and enable livelihood activities for youth and women.

 

• The scheme has an approved outlay of ₹6,600 crore for the four-year period.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• PM-DevINE does not replace existing central schemes for the Northeast but supplements them by filling development gaps.

 

• Other Northeast-focused programmes include the North East Special Infrastructure Development Scheme (NESIDS).

 

NOTE

 

• PM-NERLP (Option 1): North East Rural Livelihood Project, an earlier World Bank-assisted livelihood project, not this infrastructure scheme.

 

• PM-DRUV (Option 2): A scholarship scheme by the Ministry of Education for talented students, unrelated to Northeast infrastructure.

 

• PM-FME (Option 3): PM Formalisation of Micro Food Processing Enterprises scheme, unrelated to Northeast infrastructure funding.

question: Who was hailed as a resident dancer of Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanam for her unique contribution to the promotion of classical dance forms?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Yamini Krishnamurthy.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Yamini Krishnamurthy, an eminent Bharatanatyam and Kuchipudi exponent, was honoured as the 'Asthana Nartaki' (resident/court dancer) of the Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanam (TTD) for her contribution to classical dance. (यामिनी कृष्णमूर्ति — तिरुमाला तिरुपति देवस्थानम की आस्थान नर्तकी)

 

• She trained under legendary gurus and was a recipient of the Padma Shri (1968), Padma Bhushan (2001) and Padma Vibhushan (2016).

 

• She was renowned for her mastery of both Bharatanatyam and Kuchipudi, and played a major role in popularising Kuchipudi as a solo dance form.

 

• Yamini Krishnamurthy passed away in December 2024, leaving behind a rich legacy of classical dance revival.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• TTD (Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanam) manages the Sri Venkateswara Temple at Tirumala and patronises numerous cultural and religious institutions.

 

• The title 'Asthana Nartaki' denotes an artist formally attached to a temple/royal court to perform in its honour.

 

NOTE

 

• Uma Sharma (Option 1): A noted Kathak dancer, not associated with this TTD honour.

 

• Rukmini Devi (Option 2): Rukmini Devi Arundale was a pioneer of Bharatanatyam and founder of Kalakshetra, not the TTD resident dancer.

 

• Ragini Devi (Option 4): An American-born pioneer of Indian classical dance revival in the early 20th century, unrelated to this TTD title.

question: In February 2021, through which of the following cases did the Supreme court rule that in the cases when the Juvenile offender is under 18 years and above 16 years, he/she should be remitted to jurisdictional Juvenile Justice Board?
option_1: Rahul Sharma v. National Insurance Company Ltd
option_2: Satbir Singh v. State of Haryana
option_3: Laxmibai Chandaragi v. The State of Karnataka
option_4: Devilal v. State of Madhya Pradesh
solution_text:
The correct answer is Devilal v. State of Madhya Pradesh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In February 2021, in Devilal v. State of Madhya Pradesh (2021) 5 SCC 292, the Supreme Court held that if an accused claims to be a juvenile (16-18 years) and this issue was not raised or examined at trial, the matter should be remitted to the jurisdictional Juvenile Justice Board (JJB). (देवीलाल बनाम मध्य प्रदेश राज्य — किशोर न्याय बोर्ड)

 

• The ruling reaffirmed that a claim of juvenility can be raised at any stage of proceedings, even after final disposal, under Section 9 of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015.

 

• The Bench directed that the JJB determine the age and, where the person was aged 16-18 at the time of the offence, deal with the case in accordance with the JJ Act's provisions on heinous offences.

 

• This case reinforced the protective, rehabilitative approach of India's juvenile justice framework rather than treating age determination as a mere technicality.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015 allows a 16-18 year old accused of a heinous offence to be tried as an adult only after a preliminary assessment by the JJB.

 

• The Nirbhaya case (2012) was a major trigger for stricter provisions regarding juveniles in the 2015 Act.

 

NOTE

 

• Rahul Sharma v. National Insurance Company Ltd (Option 1): A motor accident compensation case, unrelated to juvenile justice.

 

• Satbir Singh v. State of Haryana (Option 2): A 2021 Supreme Court judgment on dowry death (Section 304B IPC), not on juvenile justice.

 

• Laxmibai Chandaragi v. The State of Karnataka (Option 3): A 2021 case concerning protection for an inter-caste married couple, unrelated to juvenile justice.

question: Which part of the Constitution of India contains the provisions of Union Executive?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Part V.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Part V of the Constitution of India, titled 'The Union', contains the provisions relating to the Union Executive, covering Articles 52 to 78. (भाग V — संघ की कार्यपालिका)

 

• Part V deals with the President, Vice-President, Council of Ministers, Attorney General, and the Union Legislature (Parliament).

 

• The Union Executive comprises the President (Article 52) as the head of state, the Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister (Article 74) to aid and advise the President, and the Attorney General of India (Article 76).

 

• Executive power of the Union is vested in the President under Article 53, exercised on the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part VI of the Constitution deals with the State Executive and State Legislature (Governor, Chief Minister, State Council of Ministers).

 

• Part III contains Fundamental Rights, while Part IV contains the Directive Principles of State Policy.

 

NOTE

 

• Part III (Option 2): Deals with Fundamental Rights (Articles 12-35), not the Union Executive.

 

• Part IV (Option 3): Deals with Directive Principles of State Policy (Articles 36-51), not the Union Executive.

 

• Part VI (Option 4): Deals with the State Executive and State Legislature, not the Union Executive.

question: Which of the following countries won the highest number of gold medals in the Tokyo Paralympic 2020?
solution_text:
The correct answer is China.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• China topped the medal tally at the Tokyo Paralympics 2020 (held in 2021) with 96 gold medals, finishing 1st overall with 207 total medals. (टोक्यो पैरालंपिक 2020 — चीन शीर्ष पर)

 

• Great Britain finished 2nd with 41 gold medals, and the United States finished 3rd with 37 gold medals.

 

• India put up its best-ever Paralympic performance, finishing 24th with 5 gold, 8 silver and 6 bronze medals (19 total).

 

• China has topped the Paralympic gold medal tally at every Summer Paralympics since 2004 (Athens).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's star performers at Tokyo 2020 Paralympics included Avani Lekhara (shooting gold), Sumit Antil (javelin gold), and Krishna Nagar (badminton gold).

 

• The Tokyo 2020 Paralympics were held from 24 August to 5 September 2021, delayed by a year due to COVID-19, just like the Olympics.

 

NOTE

 

• Australia (Option 1): Finished well down the gold medal table, not among the top nations.

 

• India (Option 2): Recorded its best-ever performance but finished 24th, far below the top gold medal winners.

 

• USA (Option 4): Finished 3rd in gold medals, behind China and Great Britain.

question: Which of the following countries has hosted the three Asian Games?
solution_text:
The correct answer is South Korea.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• South Korea has hosted the Asian Games three times: Seoul (1986), Busan (2002) and Incheon (2014). (दक्षिण कोरिया — तीन बार एशियाई खेलों की मेजबानी)

 

• The Asian Games are a multi-sport event held every four years among athletes from across Asia, organised by the Olympic Council of Asia (OCA).

 

• The first Asian Games were held in New Delhi, India, in 1951; India also hosted the 1982 Asian Games in New Delhi (twice in total).

 

• Thailand (Bangkok) has hosted the Asian Games the most number of times, four times (1966, 1970, 1978, 1998).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Japan has hosted the Asian Games twice — Tokyo (1958) and Hiroshima (1994).

 

• The 19th Asian Games were held in Hangzhou, China, in 2023.

 

NOTE

 

• Philippines (Option 2): Hosted the Asian Games only once, in Manila (1954).

 

• Japan (Option 3): Has hosted the Asian Games twice (1958, 1994), not three times.

 

• India (Option 4): Has hosted the Asian Games twice, in New Delhi (1951 and 1982), not three times.

question: Who led the English army in the Battle of Buxar?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Hector Munro.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Battle of Buxar (1764) was fought between the forces of the British East India Company, led by Major Hector Munro, and the combined armies of Mir Qasim (Nawab of Bengal), Shuja-ud-Daulah (Nawab of Awadh) and Mughal Emperor Shah Alam II. (बक्सर का युद्ध — हेक्टर मुनरो)

 

• The British emerged victorious, and the battle's outcome led to the Treaty of Allahabad (1765), under which the Company obtained the Diwani (revenue collection rights) of Bengal, Bihar and Odisha.

 

• The Battle of Buxar is considered more decisive than the Battle of Plassey (1757) in establishing British political and economic supremacy in eastern India, as it defeated a combined force of three major powers.

 

• It was fought on 22 October 1764 near Buxar, on the banks of the Ganga in present-day Bihar.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Robert Clive led the British forces at the earlier Battle of Plassey (1757) against Siraj-ud-Daulah.

 

• The Treaty of Allahabad (1765) was signed by Robert Clive with Shah Alam II and Shuja-ud-Daulah following the Battle of Buxar.

 

NOTE

 

• Lord Clive (Option 1): Led the British at the Battle of Plassey (1757) and later negotiated the Treaty of Allahabad, but did not lead the army at Buxar.

 

• William Henry Sleeman (Option 2): A 19th-century British administrator known for suppressing Thuggee, unconnected with the Battle of Buxar.

 

• Charles Eyrecoot (Eyre Coote) (Option 4): A British general known for victories like Wandiwash (1760) in South India, not the commander at Buxar.

question: Which of the following amendments to the Indian Constitution made the Right to Property a Legal Right in place of a Fundamental Right?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 44th.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978 removed the Right to Property from the list of Fundamental Rights (omitting Article 31) and made it a legal/constitutional right under Article 300A in Part XII. (44वां संविधान संशोधन — संपत्ति का अधिकार)

 

• This amendment was enacted during the Morarji Desai-led Janata Party government, largely to undo certain excesses of the 42nd Amendment passed during the Emergency.

 

• As a legal right, the Right to Property can be curtailed by an ordinary law of Parliament, whereas as a Fundamental Right it could only be restricted through a constitutional amendment.

 

• The 44th Amendment also strengthened safeguards against future declarations of Emergency, replacing 'internal disturbance' with 'armed rebellion' as grounds for Article 352.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 42nd Amendment Act, 1976 is called the 'Mini Constitution' for the sweeping changes it made, including adding 'Socialist', 'Secular' and 'Integrity' to the Preamble.

 

• Article 300A states: 'No person shall be deprived of his property save by authority of law.'

 

NOTE

 

• 40th Amendment (Option 1): Related to territorial waters, continental shelf and exclusive economic zone of India, unrelated to the Right to Property.

 

• 48th Amendment (Option 2): Related to President's Rule in Punjab, unrelated to the Right to Property.

 

• 45th Amendment (Option 4): Concerned the extension of reservation for SCs/STs and Anglo-Indians, not the Right to Property.

question: Changai dance is associated with which Indian state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nagaland.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Changai dance (also known in related forms as Changsang/Chang-Lo) is a traditional folk dance of the Chang tribe of Nagaland. (चांगई नृत्य — नागालैंड)

 

• It is performed by the Chang Naga community, primarily concentrated in the Tuensang district of Nagaland, usually during festivals and celebratory occasions.

 

• The dance is characterised by vigorous, synchronised movements accompanied by traditional songs and chants, reflecting the martial and communal spirit of the Chang Nagas.

 

• Nagaland is renowned for its rich tribal dance traditions, celebrated prominently at the annual Hornbill Festival.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other well-known folk dances of Nagaland include the Zeliang dance, Rengma dance, and Sadal Kekai (Ao tribe).

 

• Nagaland's capital is Kohima, and the state is home to numerous Naga tribes, each with distinct customs, attire and dance forms.

 

NOTE

 

• Madhya Pradesh (Option 1): Known for folk dances like Gaur Maria and Karma, not Changai.

 

• Maharashtra (Option 2): Known for Lavani and Koli dance, not Changai.

 

• Jharkhand (Option 4): Known for Chhau and Karma dance, not Changai.

question: Which is the national fruit of Bangladesh?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jackfruit.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Jackfruit (Kathal) is the national fruit of Bangladesh, prized for its size, taste and versatility in the local cuisine. (कटहल — बांग्लादेश का राष्ट्रीय फल)

 

• Bangladesh is one of the world's largest producers of jackfruit, which grows abundantly across the country due to its favourable tropical climate.

 

• The national flower of Bangladesh is the water lily (Shapla), and the national bird is the Oriental magpie-robin (Doel).

 

• Jackfruit is also grown extensively in India, particularly in Kerala (where it is the state fruit) and other southern states.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mango is the national fruit of India and also of Pakistan and the Philippines.

 

• Bangladesh's national tree is the mango tree, while jackfruit holds the distinct title of national fruit.

 

NOTE

 

• Pomegranate (Option 1): Not the national fruit of Bangladesh.

 

• Mango (Option 2): National fruit of India, not Bangladesh.

 

• Apple (Option 3): Not associated with Bangladesh as a national symbol; it is not even a major crop there.

question: Which of the following chemicals is used as a preservative to slow browning and discolouration in foods and beverages during preparation, storage and distribution?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sulphites.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sulphites (such as sodium sulphite, sodium metabisulphite and sulphur dioxide) are used as preservatives/antioxidants to slow enzymatic and non-enzymatic browning and discolouration in foods and beverages. (सल्फाइट्स — खाद्य परिरक्षक)

 

• They act by inhibiting the enzyme polyphenol oxidase, which is responsible for browning in cut fruits, vegetables and dried products, and also inhibit microbial growth.

 

• Sulphites are commonly used in dried fruits, wine, fruit juices, and processed potatoes to maintain colour and extend shelf life.

 

• They are also used as antimicrobial agents, preventing spoilage by bacteria, yeasts and moulds during storage and transport.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Excess consumption of sulphites can trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals, so food labelling regulations require their disclosure.

 

• Other common food preservatives include sodium benzoate, potassium sorbate, and citric acid.

 

NOTE

 

• Nitrous oxide (Option 1): Used mainly as a propellant (e.g., in whipped cream canisters) and as an anaesthetic, not as an anti-browning preservative.

 

• Phosgene (Option 2): A highly toxic industrial chemical and chemical warfare agent, not used in food.

 

• Chlorine (Option 4): Used mainly for water disinfection and as a bleaching/sanitising agent, not primarily as a food anti-browning preservative.

question: Which of the following reforming societies believed Vedas to be the fountain of all the knowledge?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Arya Samaj.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Arya Samaj, founded by Swami Dayanand Saraswati in 1875 in Bombay, believed the Vedas to be the fountain/source of all true knowledge and infallible. (आर्य समाज — वेदों की ओर लौटो)

 

• Its motto was 'Back to the Vedas', and it rejected idol worship, caste rigidity and ritualism, calling instead for a return to the pure Vedic religion.

 

• Dayanand Saraswati propagated his ideas through his seminal work 'Satyarth Prakash' (The Light of Truth).

 

• The Arya Samaj also promoted social reforms such as the Shuddhi movement (reconversion), widow remarriage, women's education, and opposition to child marriage.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Arya Samaj established the Dayanand Anglo-Vedic (DAV) educational institutions to promote modern education alongside Vedic learning.

 

• The Gurukul Kangri at Haridwar, founded in 1902, was another important educational initiative inspired by Arya Samaj ideals.

 

NOTE

 

• Theosophical Society (Option 1): Founded by Madame Blavatsky and Colonel Olcott in 1875 in the USA; it emphasised universal brotherhood and study of comparative religion, not exclusively Vedic supremacy.

 

• Prarthana Samaj (Option 2): Founded by Atmaram Pandurang in 1867 in Bombay, focused on monotheism and social reform, without the Arya Samaj's specific Vedic infallibility doctrine.

 

• Brahmo Samaj (Option 4): Founded by Raja Ram Mohan Roy, it emphasised monotheistic worship based on the Upanishads and rejected many later Vedic rituals rather than treating the Vedas as the ultimate authority.

question: Which of the following pairs of musicians and their instruments is INCORRECT?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pt. Ram Narayan – Sarod.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pandit Ram Narayan was a legendary maestro of the Sarangi, not the Sarod — he is widely credited with elevating the sarangi to a solo concert instrument. (पंडित राम नारायण — सारंगी वादक)

 

• He was honoured with the Padma Vibhushan (2005) for his contribution to Hindustani classical music through the sarangi.

 

• The pairing 'Pt. Ram Narayan – Sarod' is therefore factually incorrect, making this the answer to the question asking for the INCORRECT pair.

 

• The Sarod is instead associated with maestros like Ustad Ali Akbar Khan and Amjad Ali Khan.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Bismillah Khan was renowned worldwide for playing the Shehnai and was awarded the Bharat Ratna in 2001.

 

• N. Rajam is celebrated as a pioneering female exponent of the Hindustani violin tradition.

 

NOTE

 

• Bismillah Khan – Shehnai (Option 1): This pairing is correct; hence not the answer.

 

• N Rajam – Violin (Option 3): This pairing is correct; hence not the answer.

 

• Pt. Ravi Shankar – Sitar (Option 4): This pairing is correct; Ravi Shankar was a globally celebrated sitar maestro; hence not the answer.

question: The Second Five-Year Plan (1956-61) had a major goal of achieving which of the following targets?
option_3: Rapid industrialisation with focus on heavy industries
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rapid industrialisation with focus on heavy industries.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Second Five-Year Plan (1956-61) focused on rapid industrialisation, with special emphasis on the development of heavy and basic industries. (द्वितीय पंचवर्षीय योजना — भारी उद्योगों पर बल)

 

• It was based on the P.C. Mahalanobis model, which prioritised investment in capital goods and heavy industries to build a strong industrial base for long-term growth.

 

• Major public sector steel plants at Bhilai, Durgapur and Rourkela were established during this plan period with foreign collaboration.

 

• This plan is often referred to as the 'Mahalanobis Plan' or the 'Industrialisation Plan'.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The First Five-Year Plan (1951-56) focused on agriculture and was based on the Harrod-Domar model.

 

• The Third Five-Year Plan (1961-66) aimed at making the economy self-reliant and self-generating.

 

NOTE

 

• Self-reliant and self-generating economy (Option 1): This was a key goal of the Third Five-Year Plan, not the Second.

 

• Growth with stability (Option 2): This was emphasised in the Third Five-Year Plan, alongside self-reliance.

 

• Growth with social justice (Option 4): This was a broader goal associated with later plans (such as the Sixth Plan), not specifically the Second Plan's defining focus.

question: Seismograph is used to measure:
solution_text:
The correct answer is earthquakes.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A seismograph (seismometer) is an instrument used to detect and record the vibrations/tremors caused by earthquakes and other seismic waves. (भूकंपमापी — भूकंप मापन)

 

• It records ground motion as a seismogram, showing the arrival and magnitude of seismic waves (P-waves and S-waves) generated by an earthquake.

 

• The intensity/magnitude of earthquakes is measured using scales such as the Richter scale (magnitude) and the Modified Mercalli Intensity scale.

 

• Seismographs are installed at seismological observatories worldwide and are crucial for earthquake monitoring, tsunami warning systems, and studying the Earth's interior.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• A rain gauge (pluviometer) is used to measure rainfall/precipitation.

 

• A hygrometer measures atmospheric humidity, while a barometer measures atmospheric pressure.

 

NOTE

 

• Rain precipitation (Option 1): Measured using a rain gauge, not a seismograph.

 

• Underground water level (Option 2): Measured using a piezometer or water-level indicator, not a seismograph.

 

• Underground mineral content (Option 4): Assessed through geological surveys and instruments like magnetometers/gravimeters, not a seismograph.

question: This event is celebrated to mark the resurrection of Christ. Identify the event.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Easter.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Easter is the Christian festival celebrated to mark the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead, three days after his crucifixion. (ईस्टर — ईसा मसीह का पुनरुत्थान)

 

• It is considered the most important festival in the Christian calendar, marking the culmination of Holy Week.

 

• Easter is a movable feast, celebrated on the first Sunday after the first full moon following the spring (vernal) equinox, usually falling in March or April.

 

• The period of 40 days leading up to Easter, observed through fasting and penance, is called Lent.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Christmas commemorates the birth of Jesus Christ, celebrated on 25 December.

 

• Good Friday, observed on the Friday before Easter, commemorates the crucifixion of Jesus Christ.

 

NOTE

 

• Christmas (Option 2): Marks Christ's birth, not his resurrection.

 

• Holy Thursday (Option 3): Commemorates the Last Supper of Jesus with his disciples, not the resurrection.

 

• Good Friday (Option 4): Marks Christ's crucifixion and death, the event preceding the resurrection, not the resurrection itself.

question: Which of the following is another name for starch found mainly in the pulp of seeds, fruits, tubers, roots and stems of plants, especially in corn, potatoes, wheat and rice?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Amylum.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Starch is also known as Amylum, a complex carbohydrate (polysaccharide) made up of glucose units, found abundantly in the pulp of seeds, fruits, tubers, roots and stems. (एमाइलम — स्टार्च का अन्य नाम)

 

• Starch consists of two components: amylose (linear chains) and amylopectin (branched chains).

 

• It serves as the primary energy storage carbohydrate in plants and is a major dietary source of carbohydrates for humans, abundant in corn, potatoes, wheat and rice.

 

• The term 'amylum' derives from the Latin/Greek roots referring to starch, and is the root of terms like 'amylase' (the enzyme that breaks down starch).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Amylase enzymes (like salivary and pancreatic amylase) break down starch into simpler sugars during digestion.

 

• Starch turns blue-black in colour when tested with iodine solution, a standard laboratory test for its presence.

 

NOTE

 

• Xanthan (Option 2): Refers to xanthan gum, a polysaccharide produced by bacterial fermentation, used as a food thickener; not another name for starch.

 

• Olestra (Option 3): A synthetic fat substitute used in food products, unrelated to starch.

 

• Saponin (Option 4): A class of plant glycosides known for their soap-like foaming property, unrelated to starch.

question: Which of the following systems of the Delhi sultanate had a influence on the Bahmani and Vijayanagar kingdoms?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Iqtadari.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Iqtadari (Iqta) system of the Delhi Sultanate, under which land revenue assignments (iqtas) were given to nobles/officers (muqtis/walis) in lieu of cash salary, influenced the administrative systems of the Bahmani and Vijayanagar kingdoms. (इक्तादारी व्यवस्था — दिल्ली सल्तनत)

 

• The Iqta system was introduced by Iltutmish and refined further by later Sultans, including Balban and Alauddin Khalji, forming the backbone of Sultanate administration.

 

• Both the Bahmani Sultanate (Deccan Muslim kingdom) and the Vijayanagar Empire (Hindu kingdom) adopted comparable revenue-assignment/land-grant administrative practices influenced by the iqta model, adapting it to their own regional needs (e.g., Vijayanagar's Nayankara/Amaram systems shared conceptual parallels).

 

• Under the iqta system, the holder (muqti) collected revenue from the assigned territory, retained a portion for administrative/military expenses, and remitted the surplus to the central treasury.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Muhammad bin Tughlaq later increased central control over the iqta system by strengthening the office of accounting (diwan-i-wizarat) over provincial revenue.

 

• The Vijayanagar Empire's Amaram/Nayankara system parallels the iqta system in granting land in exchange for military/administrative service.

 

NOTE

 

• Walis (Option 1): Refers to governors/officers who administered iqtas, a role within the iqta system rather than the overarching system itself.

 

• Cahalgani (Option 2): Refers to the 'Chahalgani' or 'Group of Forty', the nobility of Turkish slave-officers under Iltutmish, an elite political group, not an administrative revenue system.

 

• Bitikchi (Option 3): Refers to a scribe/accountant official in the Sultanate administration, not the broader revenue-assignment system.

question: What is the product formed when CH₃CH₂OH reacts with O₂?
solution_text:
The correct answer is CO₂ + H₂O + heat and light.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ethanol (CH₃CH₂OH) undergoes complete combustion in the presence of excess oxygen (O₂) to form carbon dioxide, water, along with the release of heat and light. (एथेनॉल का दहन — CO₂ + H₂O + ऊष्मा और प्रकाश)

 

• The balanced combustion reaction is: CH₃CH₂OH + 3O₂ → 2CO₂ + 3H₂O + heat and light.

 

• This is an exothermic combustion reaction; like the burning of other hydrocarbons/alcohols, it produces a visible flame (light) along with heat, characteristic of combustion reactions.

 

• Ethanol is widely used as a biofuel and fuel additive (e.g., in petrol blending) precisely because of this high-energy combustion reaction.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Incomplete combustion of ethanol (with insufficient oxygen) can produce carbon monoxide (CO) or soot (carbon) instead of complete CO₂.

 

• Ethanol is manufactured commercially by the fermentation of sugars using yeast, or industrially by the hydration of ethene.

 

NOTE

 

• H₂O + heat (Option 1): Incomplete; omits the carbon dioxide and light produced in ethanol combustion.

 

• CO₂ + H₂O + light (Option 3): Incomplete; combustion reactions release heat in addition to light, which this option omits.

 

• CO₂ + heat and light (Option 4): Incomplete; omits water, which is also a product of ethanol combustion.

question: What was the function of an officer called Samaharta?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tax assessment.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Samaharta was a high-ranking officer in the Mauryan administration, responsible for the assessment and collection of revenue/taxes across the empire. (समाहर्ता — कर निर्धारण और संग्रहण अधिकारी)

 

• The Samaharta functioned as the chief revenue collector, overseeing the assessment of land revenue and other taxes, and worked in coordination with the Sannidhata (treasurer, who stored the collected revenue).

 

• This administrative structure is described in detail in Kautilya's Arthashastra, the ancient treatise on statecraft and economic policy of the Mauryan period.

 

• The Samaharta's duties included supervising provincial revenue officials and ensuring accurate assessment of dues from agriculture, trade and other sources.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Sannidhata was the officer in charge of the royal treasury, distinct from the Samaharta who handled assessment/collection.

 

• Other notable Mauryan administrative officers mentioned in the Arthashastra include the Amatya (minister) and Purohita (chief priest/advisor).

 

NOTE

 

• Reserve the state treasury (Option 1): This was the function of the Sannidhata, not the Samaharta.

 

• Security assurance (Option 3): Not the function of the Samaharta; internal/external security was handled by separate military and police officials.

 

• To correspond (Option 4): Not the function of the Samaharta; record-keeping/correspondence duties were handled by scribes and other officials.
